chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a person in Ihram who trod on an egg of a sand grouse and broke it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should send a stallion for the number of eggs from the sheep, just as he sends the stallion for the number of ostrich eggs from the camels.'

key_terms.فَشَدَخَهُ: And broke it (referring to the egg)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking a bird's egg while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the fidya for breaking a sand grouse egg while in Ihram, prescribing the release of a male camel as compensation proportional to the number of eggs broken. It establishes a legal analogy (qiyas) with the known ruling for ostrich eggs, demonstrating the systematic approach of Shia jurists in deriving specific penalties from established precedents found in the Imams' teachings.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Mansour Bin Hazim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam trampling an egg of a sand grouse, so he breaks it. Heasws said: ‘He should send a stallion among the sheep regarding the number of eggs, just as he would send the stallion regarding the number of the ostrich eggs to be among the camels’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram steps on the egg of a sandgrouse and shatters it. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must send rams on ewes equal to the number of eggs affected, as in the case of the eggs of ostrich in which male camel are sent on female camels.’”
